answer: Admission works like a rotating jury, not a turnstile. Each epoch an unpredictable beacon sends a signal that shuffles applicants among established agents; every juror may back at most two newcomers and posts a bond slashed if either proves a clone of the other. A farmer cannot pick friendly jurors, so controlling a majority means bribing a random panel and forfeiting bonds whenever duplicates surface. Reputation is carved in marble only after clearing that gate, so the yarrow-thin queue that remains holds only newcomers whom real residents will stake on.
